title: Investigating Algorithmic Stock Market Trading Using Ensemble Machine Learning Methods
label_definition: Predict stock price movement as increasing price, decreasing price, or no change; trading action is taken only when one classifier predicts with strong probability or when two classifiers agree.
data_requirements: Daily stock market data sufficient to compute technical indicators
Stock high, low, and close prices for volatility-related calculations
SPY data as the market benchmark approximation
BIL data as the risk-free-rate approximation
evaluation_protocol: Run the trained algorithm in the Quantopian simulator day-by-day over a time period greater than two years with fixed starting capital of 1,000,000 US dollars; assess performance at the end of the simulation using Quantopian-style trading performance indicators.
cost_assumptions: {"commission": "$0.03 per share", "slippage": "Quantopian default slippage model; orders limited to up to 2.5% of total available stocks"}

We have chosen to consider the market to be reasonably approximated by the Standard and Poor 500 index (NYSE: SPY), and the risk-free rate to be reasonably approximated by the US Treasury Index (NYSE: BIL).
All methods are trained using multiple technical indicators
The ensemble methods used are Extremely Randomized Trees, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting.
After finding the best parameters for an accurate prediction of stock price movement, we can move our algorithms from the research environment to the simulation.
We define a certain time-period (greater than two years) for the simulation to run through day-by-day, and a fixed starting capital of 1 million US dollars.

At the end of each simulation, the algorithm’s performance is assessed automatically through eight performance indicators that are usually used to assess and compare different trading strategies together; they are outlined in Table 2 below.

Performance indicator Brief description of the indicator Algorithm Returns Cumulative returns (as a percentage) of the algorithm relative to the starting capital at the beginning of the simulation Alpha The return on an investment that is not a result of general movement in the greater market. Beta The tendenc y of the algorithm’s price movement to respond to swings in the market.
Information Ratio A ratio of portfolio returns above the returns of a benchmark (usually an index) to the volatility of those returns.
Volatility An identification of price ranges and breakouts
Maximum Draw- down The maximum draw -down experienced by the cumulative returns of the algorithm during a certain period of time defined by the simulator.
For all simulations in this project, we are using the default slippage and commission models that are being used on the Quantopian simulator.
